Layer 3: differential modules and n-periodic complexes, their split Frobenius structures, K_n(A) and D_n(A) as triangulated categories with the two-description comparison.

Layer 4: compression Delta_n, the orbit category D/[n] with Keller's universal property, Stai's full faithfulness, gradable essential image and the triangulated-hull theorem, and periodic projective resolutions with Eisenbud 6.1.

Layers 5-6: curved DG algebras and modules (the DGAInfinity prerequisite is itself barely started - no DG algebra is defined yet), the curved homotopy category, absolute/co/contra acyclicity and the three Verdier quotients, and Positselski's Theorems 7.8-7.9 comparisons.
Layers 7-8: matrix factorizations with HMF(S,w) triangulated and its Frobenius model, duality, Eisenbud's local hypersurface theorem, Orlov's HMF(S,w) = D_sg(X_0), and the reconciliation functors.

Shimura geometry: AlgebraicModuli (spaces/stacks), AbelianSchemes, FiniteFlatGroups/Dieudonne, ShimuraData, ShimuraVarieties, ShimuraCompactifications, PELModuli, PerfectoidShimuraVarieties and HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups.

The automorphic side: AdelicAlgebraicGroups, SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups, AutomorphicSpectralTheory, EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison (stabilized trace comparison), AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII, CompletedCohomologyPartII, ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces and TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure.

Its own IG.0-IG.7: central leaves as smooth subschemes with Aut(X), Igusa towers and their perfections, well-positioned subsets and Lan-Stroh partial compactifications, affineness via G-zips and Nie's minimal Ekedahl-Oort stratum, the compactified Hodge-Tate fibre theorem, the semiperversity bound Rpsi in pD^{>=d}, the boundary induction formula and the final concentration inequalities.

judgements.reason: IntegralLattices needs no new theory at all - the dual lattice, discriminant form, Nikulin overlattice correspondence and the D8+ = E8 glue are already the sorry-free tree TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ - whereas ArithmeticDirichletSeries still has to build the convergent Euler product and its logarithm, the arithmetic Perron formula, the Dirichlet-density calculus, Wiener-Ikehara and the primeNumberTheoremTransfer summit.

ClassicalGroups still needs the Weyl character formula (char V_mu = Schur polynomial, still on the frontier of the highest-weight roadmap), the GL_n highest-weight classification with its central-character step, the Schur-functor decomposition of V^{tensor d}, branching with the Gelfand-Tsetlin basis and its Z(U(gl_k)) generators, and the whole SO_n/Sp_n/O_n series; ArithmeticDirichletSeries is missing only the analytic Euler product, Perron, Dirichlet density and Wiener-Ikehara on top of an already-built 28-file tree.

Coleman must first build four theories that are wholly absent from the baseline - completed group rings Z_p[[G]] with Weierstrass theory and the Lambda-module structure theorem, locally analytic distributions and Amice's unbounded transform, the Kubota-Leopoldt p-adic L-function, and global cyclotomic units - before its own norm operator and fundamental exact sequence; ClassicalGroups already has Schur-Weyl duality, the Weyl modules, weight-space decomposition, Schur polynomials and GT patterns in TauCeti and needs the character/branching theorems on top.

Coleman's chain is about twenty layers of entirely new theory stacked nine deep (p-adic measures and completed group rings, Weierstrass/Lambda-modules, locally analytic distributions, complex special values, Kubota-Leopoldt, cyclotomic units, then the Coleman map and Theorem 12.23), with no IwasawaAlgebra or padicLFunction anywhere in the baseline; PDE is missing more raw volume (Calderon-Zygmund and BMO, Schauder, De Giorgi-Nash-Moser, the parabolic Galerkin lane) but works from a substantial floor - Rellich, Poincare, Lax-Milgram, the Dirichlet spectrum and the maximal function are already proved - and stacks only about four deep.

StablePeriodicCurved has eight of its nine layers unbuilt and they stack strictly - Happel's triangulated stable category, Gorenstein-projectives and Buchweitz's D_sg equivalence, periodic complexes and D_n, the orbit category and Stai's hull, curved DG modules (whose DGAInfinity prerequisite has not yet even defined a DG algebra), Positselski's co/contra/absolute derived categories, then matrix factorizations with Eisenbud and Orlov; PDE's missing lanes (Calderon-Zygmund/BMO, Schauder, De Giorgi-Nash-Moser, Bochner spaces and Galerkin) are comparable in volume but largely parallel and sit on a finished Lane D.

AbelianSchemes cannot even state its targets until algebraic spaces, algebraic stacks, Hilbert/Quot schemes and Artin representability exist (AlgebraicModuli R09.1-R09.6), and its A2-A4 then need Raynaud's algebraic-space-to-scheme theorem, Cartier duality, Dieudonne theory, Grothendieck-Messing and Serre-Tate - a 53-stage closure fourteen deep with no algebraicSpace, pDivisible or crystalline declaration in the baseline; StablePeriodicCurved works entirely inside homological algebra on an existing exact-structure and triangulated floor.

AbelianSchemes imports AlgebraicModuli R09.1-R09.6 and A0-extension wholesale and then adds abelian schemes with rigidity and the cube, the dual via Raynaud's theorem, Weil pairings, relative H^1_dR with Gauss-Manin, Grothendieck-Messing and Serre-Tate (hence Dieudonne theory, crystalline and derived de Rham cohomology) and complex uniformization; AlgebraicModuli's only theory outside that is the characteristic-zero resolution branch R09.7a-d.

FiniteFields FF.2 cannot state the Weil/Deligne square-root bounds without l-adic etale cohomology with compact support, the Grothendieck-Lefschetz trace formula, the Weil conjectures, Weil II purity, perverse sheaves and Lefschetz pencils - none of which exists in the baseline - and it also needs SchemeAndStackFoundations plus AlgebraicModuli's own spaces and stacks beneath; AlgebraicModuli's extra work is only its resolution-of-singularities and Artin-algebraization branch.

FiniteFields imports the entire cohomological point-counting and Weil II stack (etale base change, trace formula, weights and purity, etale duality with perverse sheaves, vanishing cycles) on top of scheme and stack foundations, a 58-stage closure twenty-five deep; AutomorphicForms needs a large but shallower stack - adelic groups with Siegel sets, smooth representations of local groups, (g,K)-modules with Bernstein-Krotz globalization and van Est, plus modular curves and the complex comparison.

Drinfeld's foundations are largely present - Mathlib SkewPolynomial for L{tau}, TauCeti's function-field Riemann-Roch and divisors, adele rings - so only scheme/stack descent and its own nine layers are new; AutomorphicForms must build from nothing the smooth representation theory of locally profinite groups with Hecke algebras and Jacquet functors, adelic reduction theory and Siegel sets, (g,K)-modules with smooth moderate-growth globalization and van Est's theorem, plus ModularCurvesPartII and ComplexComparisonPartII beneath.

FiniteFlatGroups needs crystalline cohomology, derived de Rham cohomology, period rings and admissible modules, perfectoid spaces and the enhanced derived-sheaf formalism before Dieudonne theory, Fontaine-Laffaille and Breuil-Kisin can even be stated, and algebraic spaces and abelian schemes underneath that (37 stages, thirteen deep); Drinfeld builds on function-field Riemann-Roch and Ore rings that the baseline largely already has, with only descent/stack foundations plus its own layers new.

FiniteFlatGroups' whole 37-stage closure sits inside PadicFamilies', which then adds 351 further stages - Iwasawa algebras and locally analytic distributions, integral modular curves, eigenvariety and Fredholm theory, Galois deformations, Kato's Euler system, Selmer and phi-Gamma cohomology and algebraic K-theory - to reach Hida/Coleman families and their L-functions.

The two share a 277-stage core of Shimura, perfectoid and etale machinery, but PadicFamilies needs about twice as much on top of it: Iwasawa algebras and locally analytic distributions, Kubota-Leopoldt and Coleman power series, modular symbols and 18 stages of integral modular curves, phi-Gamma modules, Selmer complexes, Kato's Euler system and algebraic K-theory, against Igusa's extra perfectoid Shimura varieties, Hodge-Tate/canonical subgroups, completed cohomology and torsion-cohomology infrastructure.

Igusa's closure already contains most of AutomorphicForms (adelic groups, smooth local representations, the automorphic spaces) and then adds three hundred more stages - PEL moduli and Shimura compactifications, perfectoid Shimura varieties and the Hodge-Tate period map, diamonds with the six operations, perverse sheaves and vanishing cycles, endoscopic trace comparison - before its own Caraiani-Scholze concentration theorems.

FiniteFields must import l-adic etale cohomology, the trace formula, the Weil conjectures and Deligne's Weil II, with perverse sheaves and Lefschetz pencils, on top of scheme and stack foundations, none of it in the baseline; ClassicalGroups already has Schur-Weyl duality, Weyl modules, weight decompositions, Schur polynomials and Gelfand-Tsetlin patterns and needs only the character, dimension, branching and orthogonal/symplectic theorems above them.

PDE still has two whole lanes untouched - elliptic regularity (interior H^k, W^{2,p}, Schauder, De Giorgi-Nash-Moser) and the parabolic lane (Bochner spaces, the Gelfand triple, Galerkin, the heat semigroup) - plus Calderon-Zygmund theory, BMO and John-Nirenberg, Riesz-Thorin, the trace and extension operators and Perron's method; ArithmeticDirichletSeries needs only the convergent Euler product, arithmetic Perron, Dirichlet density and Wiener-Ikehara above its already-built 28-file tree.

PadicFamilies' closure contains all but two of AlgebraicModuli's stages and adds nearly four hundred more - Iwasawa algebras and locally analytic distributions, integral modular curves and their Galois representations, p-adic Hodge theory and crystalline cohomology, eigenvarieties, Selmer and phi-Gamma cohomology and Kato's Euler system - before Hida/Coleman families can be stated.

FiniteFlatGroups' entire closure is contained in Igusa's, which then adds close to three hundred stages: perfectoid spaces and diamonds with the six operations, etale duality and perverse sheaves, PEL moduli and Shimura compactifications, the Hodge-Tate period map, endoscopic trace comparison and completed cohomology, before the Caraiani-Scholze semiperversity and torsion-concentration arguments.

AbelianSchemes needs algebraic spaces, stacks, Hilbert/Quot and Artin representability, then Raynaud's theorem for the dual, Cartier duality and Weil pairings, Dieudonne theory with Grothendieck-Messing and Serre-Tate, and the complex Hodge comparison - a 53-stage closure with no algebraicSpace or pDivisible in the baseline; Drinfeld starts from Ore rings and function-field Riemann-Roch that already exist and adds descent/stack foundations plus its own uniformization, moduli and t-motive layers.

Coleman has to construct four separate absent theories before its own layers - locally analytic distributions with the Amice transforms, completed group rings with Weierstrass theory and the Lambda-module structure theorem, the Kubota-Leopoldt p-adic L-function, and global cyclotomic units with the index formula - about twenty-five layers with nothing named IwasawaAlgebra or padicLFunction in the baseline; StablePeriodicCurved's stack is comparably deep but its foundations (Quillen exact structures with IsFrobenius, morphism ideals, Mathlib's triangulated and derived categories) are already in place.

PDE is missing about two thirds of its milestones, including two untouched lanes - Schauder and De Giorgi-Nash-Moser regularity, and the parabolic Bochner/Galerkin/heat-semigroup lane - plus Calderon-Zygmund singular integrals, BMO and John-Nirenberg, Riesz-Thorin, trace and extension operators and Perron's method; ClassicalGroups needs roughly a dozen theorems (Weyl character and dimension, the highest-weight bijection, branching and the Gelfand-Tsetlin basis, the SO/Sp/O series) on a base that already supplies Schur-Weyl duality, Weyl modules and Schur polynomials.

AutomorphicForms already imports AlgebraicModuli R09.1-R09.5 and then adds about thirty-six further stages - adelic algebraic groups with reduction theory and Siegel sets, smooth representations of locally profinite groups with Hecke algebras, nine stages of integral modular curves, the complex GAGA/Hodge comparison, and its own (g,K)-module, van Est, constant-term and rationality layers; AlgebraicModuli's only theory outside that closure is the R09.6 algebraization and R09.7 resolution branch.

Both import a whole cohomology theory absent from the baseline, but FiniteFields needs the larger and deeper one - l-adic etale cohomology with compact support and base change, the Lefschetz trace formula, the Weil conjectures, Weil II weights and purity, etale duality with perverse sheaves and vanishing cycles (58 stages, twenty-five deep) - whereas FiniteFlatGroups needs crystalline cohomology, derived de Rham and period rings above the same algebraic-space and abelian-scheme foundations (37 stages, thirteen deep).

PadicFamilies must build Iwasawa algebras and locally analytic distributions, integral modular curves with their Galois representations, p-adic Hodge and crystalline cohomology, eigenvariety Fredholm theory and, for its arithmetic families, Selmer complexes, phi-Gamma modules and Kato's Euler system - nearly four hundred stages, forty-nine deep; Drinfeld works over a function field from Ore rings, Riemann-Roch and adeles the baseline largely already provides.
